newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican gov't proposes 17 pct minimum wage hike.
newsitem.headline: Mexican gov't proposes 17 pct minimum wage hike.

text.p: Mexico's Labor Minister Javier Bonilla said he would send on Monday a proposal to the president of the National Commission of Minimum Salaries proposing a 17 percent hike in the base wage.

The minimum wage hike was agreed between government, business and labor leaders as part of the anti-inflation "Alliance for Growth" hammered out in late October. Bonilla said it had to be ratified by the commission.

He was speaking during an assembly of trade unionists in the chemical and petrochemical industry. "The Commission has the legal and formal responsibility for fixing minimum salaries, what the Alliance does is make recommendations," a statement quoted him as saying on Sunday.
According to terms of the Alliance, the minimum wage hike is due to take effect on December 3.
